steps.title: Note your current settings
steps.detail: Write down the Wi-Fi name and password and any custom DNS because they are erased by the reset.
warnings: Resetting erases your Wi-Fi name, password and any custom settings; note them first.

steps.title: Find the reset hole
steps.detail: Look on the back panel for a small recessed hole labelled RESET.

steps.title: Power the router on
steps.detail: Plug the power adapter in and wait until the power light is steady (about two minutes). Why: A reset while the unit is still booting may not register.

steps.title: Hold the reset button
steps.detail: Press and hold the recessed button with a straightened paperclip for 10 to 15 seconds (some models need 30), then release when the lights flash. Do not let go early or the reset will not complete. Reference only, no picture on the glasses: Photo of a paperclip pressing the recessed reset hole https://www.ifixit.com/Guide/MOCK-Reset-A-Router/000000. UNCERTAIN: Step 4: only text was read, so the exact light pattern that signals the reset was NOT seen.
warnings: Use a paperclip, never a sharp pin that could snap off inside.

steps.title: Wait for the restart
steps.detail: Wait about three minutes while the router restarts and the lights settle; the case may be warm.

steps.title: Sign in with the defaults
steps.detail: Connect to the default Wi-Fi name printed on the label and sign in with the default admin password from the label.
